targets.authors: Lammers, J., Stoker, J. I., & Stapel, D. A.
targets.title: Differentiating social and personal power: Opposite effects on stereotyping, but parallel effects on behavioral approach tendencies.
targets.evidence_quote: We performed an independent, direct, and better powered (N = 295) replication of Study 1, an experiment (N = 113) by Lammers, Stoker, and Stapel (2009).
targets.outcome_quote: Our results did not replicate the effects on behavioral approach, but partially replicated the effects on stereotyping. Compared to personal power, social power produced less stereotyping, but neither form of power differed significantly from the control condition, and effect sizes were considerably lower than the original estimates.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly report partial stereotyping replication and failure on behavioral approach. Speculation about prime validity does not replace the substantive mixed verdict with an uninformative verdict.

reasoning: One new Norwegian sample directly re-tests Study 1 of the cited original paper. Other power studies are background, not targets.
